judge: Two judges, each a Claude agent shown only the match sheet's claims and truth, not which method made the claims, ruled on every claim without seeing each other's rulings. An adjudicating agent ruled on each claim where they differed. Rules: the same problem at the same place; a general claim states nothing; when unsure, no match.

matches.note: The code summary declares 6 stories, but the building has 5 floors. This is stories.
G0.1 has the same conflict between the 20,659 SF total and 19,459 SF. This is area_total.
The claim names G1.1 to G1.5 and says each shows only one stair where two are required. That covers the third, fourth and fifth floors.

The claim says the 21-inch width on the G1.3 Stair 1 marker is below the minimum and does not match the 46 inches on other floors. It gives no capacity or load. exit_capacity is about 71 people below a load of 101. I was unsure this is the same defect, so I did not match it.
On A1.2 the title block says THIRD FLOOR PLAN and the drawing label says SECOND FLOOR PLAN. This is floor_name.
The index lists A7.1 Roof Plan, and the set has no such sheet. This is index_extra.
The claim is about door ratings in the schedule. It does not mention door 2004 missing a row or the type conflict for door 4008.
The claim says Stair 1 is not drawn on the first floor plan A1.1. This is stair_discharge. It says the upper floors show the stair, so it is not stair_mid.
Room 216 on A1.2 is labeled OFFICE where it should be BEDROOM. The claim compares it with other floors instead of the finish schedule, but the room and the conflicting names are the same.
